lxc_921f2f72305ff4b0.text: The batter uses a flat bat to hit the ball.

lxc_b3a0677fd5af887a.text: When the ball is hit, the two batters at the wickets can run to each other’s end.

lxc_172045ffb0fd9cc4.text: Each completed run adds one run to the score.

lxc_b2721b098c149243.text: If the ball reaches the boundary rope around the field, the batting team gets four runs without running.

lxc_b8c64c6f16f56e3e.text: If the ball flies over the boundary without bouncing, the team gets six runs.

lxc_8f43ab0c8ec7decf.text: The bowler runs up and bowls the ball toward the batter.

lxc_7618dae7b8299e29.text: The ball may bounce once on the pitch before it reaches the batter.

lxc_7ce33f3ebaf8f92b.text: Six valid balls from one bowler make one over.

lxc_d211274d93ec083b.text: After each over, a different bowler takes the ball from the other end.

lxc_66511db03a151e39.text: One bowler cannot bowl two overs in a row.

lxc_4d79aa051366608a.text: There are several ways a batter can be dismissed.

lxc_4cd3c2c8772675c8.text: Bowled means the ball hits the stumps and the bails fall off.

lxc_30b16faee6b5c81a.text: Caught means a fielder catches a ball hit by the bat before it touches the ground.

lxc_7c41613ba092178a.text: Run out means the batter is outside the crease line when a fielder breaks the wicket with the ball during a run.

lxc_63aac87f53f85c7c.text: Ten dismissals can end an innings.

lxc_20a37028c301aec8.text: A Test match is the longest.

lxc_5bfb4c17fa94998b.text: Each team can bat in two innings, and the match can last up to five days.

lxc_46ceb85fd8f6b382.text: A One Day International, called an ODI, gives each team 50 overs to bat.

lxc_0b66009dcf74c995.text: An ODI usually finishes in one day.

lxc_168a64b94f319d98.text: A Twenty20, called a T20, gives each team only 20 overs.

lxc_d974b624edbfbd71.text: A T20 match takes about three hours.

lxc_5a64fadea168e370.text: The ICC Cricket World Cup uses ODI matches.

lxc_1f0578fcf8c3cfb4.text: The ICC Men’s T20 World Cup uses T20 matches.

lxc_6602ae95de1ea23f.text: Cricket is a sport played by two teams of eleven players.

lxc_e5ebe7c3a9de0cdc.text: One team bats, and the other team bowls and fields.

lxc_00f8e7f979f900dd.text: The game uses a bat, ball, pitch, and wickets.

lxc_f4dcb56835288408.text: Teams score runs and play in three main match formats.

lxc_5e5d0187c197bdc8.text: This explainer has at least five short parts with an immediate guided check after each part, so you can learn one idea at a time.

lxc_54a98534101142a8.text: The pitch is a flat strip of ground in the middle of the field.

lxc_17987b80ec83d5a6.text: At each end of the pitch there is a wicket.

lxc_e10e7ab879042834.text: A wicket is made of three wooden sticks called stumps.

lxc_3c9ea7064d6824da.text: Two small pieces of wood called bails sit on top of the stumps.

lxc_a9df9dc6240689b8.text: The bowler stands at one end and sends the ball toward the wicket at the other end.

lxc_afc1878d8d7c5078.text: The batter stands in front of their wicket to protect it.

lxc_753396c998f0f684.text: Cricket is played by two teams.

lxc_c549661469852d75.text: The other team fields and bowls.

lxc_1911b69914bf79fc.text: The batting team tries to score as many runs as possible.

lxc_3799c2bf582766d8.text: The fielding team tries to get the batters out.

lxc_17efab2e699f08f8.text: An innings can end when ten batters are out or when the team finishes its overs.

lxc_24893c82c2de6fb7.text: The team with more runs usually wins.
